kpis.name: Leverage ratio
kpis.explanation: Measures financial strength by comparing core equity funds to total assets.
kpis.description: The leverage ratio remains stable at 4.72% in the first two quarters, indicating prudent capital management.
kpis.signal: Stability of leverage ratio despite asset variations

kpis.name: Tier 1 capital
kpis.explanation: Amount of high-quality core equity funds held by the bank.
kpis.description: Tier 1 capital decreases from 54,689 Mln€ to 53,291 Mln€ between September 2024 and December 2024.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in core equity funds year-end

kpis.name: Total leverage exposures
kpis.explanation: Total assets used to calculate the leverage ratio.
kpis.description: Total leverage exposure slightly decreases from 1,157,950 Mln€ to 1,129,683 Mln€ between September and December 2024.
kpis.signal: Reduction in total exposure despite elevated base

kpis.name: CET1 capital
kpis.explanation: Highest-quality core equity funds, including retained earnings.
kpis.description: CET1 capital decreases from 46,824 Mln€ to 45,260 Mln€ between September and December 2024.

kpis.name: Retained earnings
kpis.explanation: Portion of profits reinvested in the company.
kpis.description: Retained earnings decline from 35,176 Mln€ to 33,070 Mln€ between September and December 2024.

kpis.name: Intangible assets
kpis.explanation: Immaterial assets such as goodwill or patents deducted from regulatory capital.
kpis.description: Intangible assets (deduction) increase from 987 Mln€ to 1,078 Mln€ between September and December 2024.

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 declared fiscal years by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.908 EUR last year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 declared fiscal years.

kpis.name: Payout ratio

risks.title: Competitive pressure from neobanks and BigTech on retail deposits
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed at top of strategic sections in ING annual report; intensive language ('significant competitive pressure', 'disruptive entrants'). Upward trend with Revolut, N26 gaining scale and GAFA entering payments. Competition category weighs heavily for a pan-European retail bank.

risks.title: AML/KYC regulatory compliance and sanctions risk
risks.score_rationale: ING paid 775 M€ in 2018 in connection with AML settlement in the Netherlands; risk remains cited as priority in every subsequent annual report with strong language ('material risk', 'ongoing regulatory scrutiny'). Stable trend but maximum severity level given historical record. Regulation category is the heaviest for European banks.

risks.title: Cyber risk and operational resilience of banking systems
risks.score_rationale: Systematically mentioned in top 5 operational risks in ING annual report; explicit language ('increasing sophistication of cyber attacks', 'critical infrastructure'). Upward trend with proliferation of sector incidents (DDoS on ING NL in 2023). Cybersecurity category in sharp progression for digital banks.

risks.title: Digital transformation and dependence on third-party technology vendors
risks.score_rationale: Technology concentration risk discussed in operational risk section; moderate language ('third-party dependency', 'cloud migration risks'). Upward trend with acceleration of Think Forward/Accelerate program. Technology category weight increasing for banks in transformation.

risks.title: Geopolitical exposure in emerging markets (Turkey, Russia)
risks.score_rationale: Geopolitical risk explicitly addressed in annual report following Ukraine war and Russia sanctions; strong language ('material exposure', 'sanctions compliance'). ING had to provision significant losses on Russian portfolio in 2022-2023. Stable trend after partial divestiture but residual risk remains.

risks.title: Non-compliance risk with CRR3/Basel IV capital requirements
risks.score_rationale: CRR3 (Basel IV implementation) effective 2025 with output floor at 72.5%; ING explicitly mentions impact on RWA in investor communications. Precise language ('significant increase in risk-weighted assets', 'capital planning uncertainty'). Upward trend with tight regulatory calendar.

risks.title: Litigation risk and multi-jurisdictional regulatory proceedings
risks.score_rationale: ING subject to proceedings in several countries (AML investigations in Italy, Australia, mortgage litigation in the Netherlands); mentioned in financial statement notes with provisions recorded. Moderate but recurring language. Stable trend with risk of additional proceedings.

risks.title: Climate risk and transition to sustainable finance (EU taxonomy)
risks.score_rationale: ING committed to carbon neutrality in lending portfolio (Terra approach); EU taxonomy and CSRD impose increasing reporting obligations. Language progressively stronger ('stranded assets', 'transition risk in lending portfolio'). Upward trend with tightening ESG regulation.
